subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup move to token-verified owner capture with dmPolicy="allowlist", or should pairing remain the default with stronger manual allowlist guidance?
rationale: This changes the default authorization boundary for a bundled channel and must balance safer defaults against first-run usability and compatibility for existing pairing-mode operators.

options.title: Adopt verified owner capture
options.body: Fresh Telegram setup would require the owner to send a displayed verification token, then store that numeric sender ID in allowFrom and use allowlist mode by default.

options.title: Keep pairing default with warnings
options.body: Leave pairing as the default and improve setup/docs warnings so private deployments manually switch to allowlist.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap design
options.body: Defer this narrow default change until the broader one-line local bootstrap and Telegram owner setup direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Adopt verified owner capture
recommendation.body: Fresh Telegram setup would require the owner to send a displayed verification token, then store that numeric sender ID in allowFrom and use allowlist mode by default.

likelyOwner.reason: History points most strongly to steipete across Telegram setup, docs, DM policy, and security-default product boundaries.
